definitions.english: Needs are things you must have. Wants are things that are nice to have.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko ke dintho tseo o tlamehang ho ba le tsona. Ditakatso ke tse monate feela.

definitions.english: A need is something you cannot do without. A want is nice to have.
definitions.sesotho: Tlhoko ke ntho eo o ke keng wa phela ntle le yona. Takatso e monate feela.

definitions.english: Needs keep you alive and safe. Wants make life fun.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko di o boloka o phela mme o sireletsehile. Ditakatso di etsa bophelo bo monate.

definitions.english: Food, water, clothes, and a home are needs. Toys and sweets are wants.
definitions.sesotho: Dijo, metsi, diaparo le lehae ke ditlhoko. Dipapadi le dipompong ke ditakatso.

definitions.english: Needs come first. Wants come after needs.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko di tla pele. Ditakatso di tla kamora ditlhoko.

definitions.english: Needs are essential expenses. Wants are discretionary purchases.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko ke ditshenyehelo tsa bohlokwa. Ditakatso ke ditheko tsa boikgethelo.

definitions.english: Distinguishing needs from wants helps prioritize spending.
definitions.sesotho: Ho khetholla ditlhoko le ditakatso ho thusa ho beha tshebediso pele.

definitions.english: Needs include food, shelter, education, and transport.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko di kenyelletsa dijo, bolulo, thuto le dipalangwang.

definitions.english: The difference is subjective but essential for budgeting.
definitions.sesotho: Phapang e itshetlehile boemong empa e bohlokwa bakeng sa tekanyetso.

definitions.english: Understanding needs vs wants enables wise resource allocation.
definitions.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa ditlhoko le ditakatso ho dumella ho arola mehlodi ka bohlale.

definitions.english: Needs are non-discretionary expenses. Wants reflect lifestyle choices.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko ke ditshenyehelo tse sa qojoeng. Ditakatso di bontsha dikgetho tsa bophelo.

definitions.english: The 50/30/20 rule allocates 50 percent to needs.
definitions.sesotho: Molao wa 50/30/20 o arola 50% ho ditlhoko.

definitions.english: Distinguishing needs from wants requires self-awareness.
definitions.sesotho: Ho khetholla ditlhoko le ditakatso ho hloka ho itseba.

definitions.english: Needs are inelastic; wants are elastic.
definitions.sesotho: Ditlhoko ha di fetohe habonolo; ditakatso di a feto-fetoha.

definitions.english: Maslow hierarchy frames needs as physiological and safety requirements.
definitions.sesotho: Maslow o hlalosa ditlhoko e le tsa mmele le tshireletso.

examples.english: School uniform = need. New toy = want.
examples.sesotho: Yunifomo ya sekolo = tlhoko. Sebapadiswa se setjha = takatso.

examples.english: A warm blanket = need. A new phone = want.
examples.sesotho: Kobo e futhumetseng = tlhoko. Fono e ntjha = takatso.

examples.english: School books = need. Comic books = want.
examples.sesotho: Dibuka tsa sekolo = tlhoko. Dibuka tsa metlae = takatso.

examples.english: Transport to school = need. Netflix = want.
examples.sesotho: Dipalangwang ho ya sekolong = tlhoko. Netflix = takatso.

examples.english: School supplies = need. Designer shoes = want.
examples.sesotho: Disebediswa tsa sekolo = tlhoko. Dieta tsa designer = takatso.

examples.english: Basic phone = need. Latest smartphone = want.
examples.sesotho: Fono ya motheo = tlhoko. Smartphone ya morao-rao = takatso.

examples.english: Nutritious food = need. Eating out = want.
examples.sesotho: Dijo tse nang le phepo = tlhoko. Ho jella kantle = takatso.

examples.english: Basic clothing = need. Brand fashion = want.
examples.sesotho: Diaparo tsa motheo = tlhoko. Feshene ya mabitso = takatso.
Rente = tlhoko. Folete e kgolo = takatso.

examples.english: Textbooks = need. Coffee shop spending = want.
examples.sesotho: Dibuka = tlhoko. Ho reka kofi = takatso.

examples.english: Data for classes = need. Streaming = want.
examples.sesotho: Data bakeng sa dithuto = tlhoko. Streaming = takatso.

examples.english: Basic groceries = need. Restaurant meals = want.
examples.sesotho: Dijo tsa motheo = tlhoko. Dijo tsa resturante = takatso.

examples.english: Laptop for studies = need. Gaming console = want.
examples.sesotho: Laptop bakeng sa dithuto = tlhoko. Gaming console = takatso.

misconceptions.english: Everything you want is a need — FALSE! Wants are optional.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ntho e nngwe le e nngwe eo o e batlang ke tlhoko — HA SE NNETE! Ditakatso ke tsa boikgethelo.

misconceptions.english: Wants are bad — FALSE! They are fine after needs.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ditakatso di mpe — HA SE NNETE! Di lokile kamora ditlhoko.

misconceptions.english: Needs are boring — FALSE! Meeting needs feels good.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ditlhoko di a tena — HA SE NNETE! Ho fihlela ditlhoko ho monate.

misconceptions.english: If I really want it, it becomes a need — FALSE!
misconceptions.sesotho: Haeba ke e batla haholo, e fetoha tlhoko — HA SE NNETE!

misconceptions.english: Expensive things are always wants — FALSE! Some needs cost a lot.
misconceptions.sesotho: Dintho tse turang ke ditakatso kamehla — HA SE NNETE! Ditlhoko tse ding di a tura.

misconceptions.english: Cheap things are always needs — FALSE! Price does not determine.
misconceptions.sesotho: Dintho tse theko e tlase ke ditlhoko — HA SE NNETE! Theko ha e etse qeto.

misconceptions.english: Lifestyle inflation is normal — FALSE! It undermines goals.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho nyoloha ha bophelo ke ntho e tlwaelehileng — HA SE NNETE! Ho senya dipakane.

misconceptions.english: All discretionary spending is bad — FALSE! Wants provide quality of life.
misconceptions.sesotho: Tshebediso yohle ya boikgethelo e mpe — HA SE NNETE! Ditakatso di ntlafatsa bophelo.

misconceptions.english: The line is always clear — FALSE! Context matters.
misconceptions.sesotho: Phapang e hlakile kamehla — HA SE NNETE! Boemo bo a bohlokwa.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to practice sorting needs from wants?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ikwetlisa ho arola ditlhoko le ditakatso?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about budgeting for needs?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka tekanyetso ya ditlhoko?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn to balance needs and wants?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ithuta ho lekalekanya ditlhoko le ditakatso?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know how to resist impulse wants?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho tseba ho hanela ditakatso tsa tshohanyetso?

how_to.english: Before buying, ask: Do I need this or just want it?
how_to.sesotho: Pele o reka, ipotse: Na ke a e hloka kapa ke a e batla?

how_to.english: Make a list of needs first, then wants.
Wait one day before buying something you want.
Categorize expenses as needs or wants.
how_to.sesotho: Arola ditshenyehelo e le ditlhoko kapa ditakatso.

how_to.english: Use the 50/30/20 rule to limit wants spending.
Wait 30 days before major want purchases.
how_to.sesotho: Ema matsatsi a 30 pele o reka.

how_to.english: Conduct a needs audit of monthly expenses.
Distinguish lifestyle inflation from genuine needs.
Practice mindful spending and delayed gratification.

why.english: Knowing needs vs wants helps you spend wisely.
why.sesotho: Ho tseba ho thusa ho sebedisa ka bohlale.

why.english: Needs come first to keep you safe.
Wants are fine after needs are met.

why.sesotho: Ho khetholla ho thusa ho beha pele.
Taolo ya ditakatso e thibela sekoloto.

why.english: Understanding needs vs wants builds discipline.
Needs analysis is foundational to budgeting.

why.sesotho: Ho sebedisa ka boomo ho eketsa kgotsofalo.

situation.english: You have M50. School shoes (M40) are worn out. You also want a new toy (M45). Which do you buy?
situation.sesotho: O na le M50. Dieta tsa sekolo (M40) di senyehile. O batla le sebapadiswa (M45). O reka sefe?

advice.english: School shoes are a NEED. The toy is a WANT. Buy the shoes.
advice.sesotho: Dieta tsa sekolo ke TLHOKO. Sebapadiswa ke TAKATSO. Reka dieta.

lesson.sesotho: Ditlhoko di tla pele ho ditakatso kamehla.

situation.english: Your phone breaks and you need it for school communication. A basic phone costs M300. A smartphone costs M1,000. Which?
situation.sesotho: Fono ya hao e senyehile mme o e hloka bakeng sa sekolo. E bonolo M300. Smartphone M1,000. E feng?

advice.english: Basic phone meets the need. Smartphone is a want unless you have extra money.
advice.sesotho: Fono e bonolo e fihlella tlhoko. Smartphone ke takatso ntle le chelete e eketsehileng.

lesson.english: Meeting needs does not require the most expensive option.
lesson.sesotho: Ho fihlella ditlhoko ha ho hloke ntho e turang haholo.

situation.english: You need a laptop for studies. Options: New MacBook M15,000 or used laptop M4,000 that meets requirements. Which?
situation.sesotho: O hloka laptop bakeng sa dithuto. MacBook M15,000 kapa e sebedisitsweng M4,000. E feng?

advice.english: Used laptop meets the need at 73% less cost. Invest the M11,000 difference.
advice.sesotho: E sebedisitsweng e fihlella tlhoko ka 73% e theko e tlase. Boloka M11,000 e setseng.

lesson.english: Meeting needs smartly frees money for savings and investments.
lesson.sesotho: Ho fihlella ditlhoko ka bohlale ho lokolla chelete bakeng sa poloko.
